newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: European bunkers stable, buyers await weakness.
newsitem.headline: European bunkers stable, buyers await weakness.

text.p: European bunker prices were broadly stable on Thursday and demand in most places was slack with buyers still feeling further price falls were imminent, dealers said.
Rotterdam 380 CST bunkers were assessed at $113/$115 fob. Dealers said price rises of $2 a tonne in the barge market had had little knock-on effect on bunkers. Demand was also slack.
Hamburg prices dipped about $1 a tonne to $118/$119 fob. The modest drop lifted demand, dealers seeming content with a combination of small and large enquiries.
Mediterranean prices were little changed from Wednesday and most ports were rather quiet. Only southern France demonstrated real signs of life.
"It's been a bit more active despite the high prices," one French dealer said.
In Fujairah, a firm Singapore bunker market and strong fuel oil cargo market kept prices high.
In Durban, sellers were once again able to offer fuel oil, after mid-week difficulties.
